rules.statement: A notary is not liable to his client in damages for loss caused by an error of judgment on the part of the notary, nor would he be chargeable with negligence if he makes a mistake on a point of law or practice as to which there was reasonable doubt.
rules.supporting_quote: It is clear law that a notary, like a solicitor, is not liable to his client in damage for loss caused to him by an error of judgment on the part of the notary, nor would he be chargeable with negligence if he make a mistake on a point of law or practice as to which there was reasonable doubt. (See Kemp v. Burt, 1 [4 Barn. & Adolp. 442.] Elkington v. Holland. 2 [9 M. & W. 659.])
